title: Unit – 1 : Session – 6 : SLO – 1  |  Process Life Cycle — Fill in the Missing Words
sections: A PROCESS is a program in execution.
A process passes through states: NEW, READY, RUNNING, WAITING (BLOCKED) and TERMINATED.
The OS creates a process and assigns it a PROCESS CONTROL BLOCK (PCB) holding its state,
program counter, registers and memory information.
The SCHEDULER (dispatcher) picks a ready process and gives it the CPU.
When a running process requests I/O it moves to the WAITING state.
After I/O completes, the process returns to the READY queue.
When a process finishes execution it is TERMINATED and its resources are deallocated.
CONTEXT SWITCHING saves the state of one process and restores the state of another.
Creation: fork()/spawn, PCB allocation, memory setup.
Scheduling: choosing which ready process runs next (short-term scheduler).
Termination: exit(), releasing memory, closing open files, removing the PCB.
